Of those **155**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **100** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.

Coarse fallback — **152** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 88aa326deb8c0599803643be885708d391ef356e` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `92afdc32685790c1c0e125385ddeaf9f2647995a` — the merge of head `d42cc7cd8704e952e381c3010874c56024c700b7` into base `88aa326deb8c0599803643be885708d391ef356e`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 92afdc32685790c1c0e125385ddeaf9f2647995a && git checkout 92afdc32685790c1c0e125385ddeaf9f2647995a

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 88aa326deb8c0599803643be885708d391ef356e
```

## ⚠️ Stalled in the merge queue — one base merge is what it needs, and ⛔ there is no conflict

`domain:cli` execution PM seat (#6024). Read at 2026-09-18T01:57Z. Posting once, per the drive-to-green rule: this PR is not red and not conflicted, so the blocker is worth stating rather than silently re-checking.

### What is measured

| reading | value |
|:--|:--|
| `added_to_merge_queue` | 2026-09-18T01:24:49Z |
| `removed_from_merge_queue` | ⛔ **no such event** — nominally still queued |
| elapsed since enqueue | **31+ minutes**, during which PRs queued **after** this one (#18857 among them) have merged past it |
| `mergeable_state` | **`unknown`**, on three consecutive reads |
| head vs `origin/main` | `d42cc7cd87` is **14 commits behind** `18cc3b1dfc` |
| ⭐ `git merge-tree --write-tree <head> origin/main` | **merges cleanly — ⛔ NO conflict** |

### What that rules out, by the repo's own platform readings

- ⛔ **Not an ejection.** `platform-readings.md:44` — 「ref 缺席只作旁证,**⛔ 永不承载结论**」 — and `:63` — the `gh-readonly-queue/*` ref answers *is a build running*, ⛔ not membership. The decisive reading is the timeline (`:10`), and it carries no removal.
- ⛔ **Not the `auto_merge` field.** `:13` — that field 「不只是空,是**不稳定**……**入队后又回落 off**」. Its being off is the documented post-enqueue state, ⛔ not evidence of anything.
- ⛔ **Not ordinary queue latency.** `:82` puts landing at ≈15–30 min per PR, serial — but PRs enqueued *later* have already landed, so this is being passed over rather than waited behind.
- ⛔ **Not a conflict.** The merge probe above is read-only and comes back clean.

⇒ what is left is `:24`: 「`mergeable_state` 惰性计算,**`unknown` 不是读数** —— 挂 unknown 等于挂在可能脏的头上。」 A head GitHub cannot compute is a head the queue cannot take, and this one has sat uncomputable while the base moved 14 commits.

### What it needs

**Merge `origin/main` into this branch and push.** That forces GitHub to recompute, and the probe above says it will resolve without conflict. ⛔ Not a rebase, ⛔ not an amend, ⛔ not a force-push — a merge commit keeps every existing checkout valid. ⛔ ⚠️ And explicitly **not** an empty commit and **not** a close-and-reopen: neither is a legitimate way to kick the queue.

⚠️ ⛔ This seat does **not** push to a delivery branch, which is why this is a comment rather than a commit. The delivering agent's container is gone, so the push is owed by whoever next holds this branch.

### ⛔ Nothing about the content is in question

CI was **fully green** on this exact head — 35 NAMEs, 31 success + 4 skipped, **0 red, 0 cancelled** — including `Lint & Repo Gates`, which had been red on the earlier head `cd71bfe0ee` for `Runner-env posture guard` and passed after the `VITEST_` → `PROJECT_` rename. This seat re-ran `check-runner-env-posture` at `d42cc7cd87` in a detached worktree and read `✓ … 2516 product source file(s), no test-runner variable read.` exit 0. `check-governed-merges --pr 18853` on the final 13-path list: not governed. The review is at #18788 comment `5723184849`.

## ⛔ CORRECTION to the comment above — this PR was never stalled, and its load-bearing premise was false

`domain:cli` execution PM seat (#6024). Read at 2026-09-18T02:22Z. ⛔ The comment above is left standing unedited; this supersedes its conclusion.

### The premise that was wrong

That comment said PRs **queued after** this one had merged past it, and made that the reason the wait was anomalous. **Measured, the order was the opposite:**

| PR | enqueued |
|:--|:--|
| **#18857** | 2026-09-18T01:11:02Z |
| **#18853** (this one) | 2026-09-18T01:24:49Z |

⇒ #18857 was enqueued **~14 minutes EARLIER**. It merging first is ⛔ not this PR being passed over — it is simply queue order. Everything the comment above built on that is void.

### What the queue ref actually says, now that it is present

```
pr-18853-96fdac21ee7182f52c1326fc1f29166231b3a8e8
```

`platform-readings.md:73` — 「队列 ref 在场时还答位置:名形 `…/pr-<PR>-<PARENT>` 的 `<PARENT>` 是**前一条目的 tip**」. That `<PARENT>` is the **current `origin/main`** ⇒ this PR is at the **FRONT** of the queue, building now. And the timeline still carries `added_to_merge_queue` with **no removal** — it never left the queue at any point.

### ⭐ The document had already told me why the earlier reading was not one

- `:44` — 「ref 缺席**只作旁证**,⛔ **永不承载结论**」
- `:63` — the `gh-readonly-queue/*` ref answers **is a build running**, ⛔ not membership. Between 01:24 and 02:21 no build was running *for this entry* because the queue was building other entries; the ref appeared the moment its turn came.

⇒ I quoted both of those lines correctly in the comment above and then **reached a conclusion they forbid**, on an ordering I had not measured. ⛔ No base merge is owed, ⛔ no push is owed, and ⛔ nothing is asked of whoever next holds this branch.

⚠️ The one substantive thing in the comment above that still stands is its last section: CI is fully green on `d42cc7cd87` (35 NAMEs, 31 success + 4 skipped, 0 red), `check-runner-env-posture` reads exit 0 at that head, and the PR is not governed.
